name: IMRC
mission: Indian Muslim Relief and Charities (IMRC) is dedicated to alleviating poverty in India. The donations it raises, from individuals throughout the United States, fund its charitable projects in India. Even the smallest of donations can greatly benefit an orphaned child or a widowed woman. Charity has always been an integral aspect of a Muslim society. The Quran places great emphasis on giving to the poor, and our beloved Prophet (pbuh) is reported to have said that wealth does not diminish by charity. When you donate to IMRC, you are supporting a network of more than 100 Muslim organizations in India. These organizations provide educational and financial support to thousands of orphans, destitute children and needy families. Your generous donations also support medical clinics, women's training centers and other social welfare institutions.

strengths.detail: IMRC demonstrates elite fiscal management with a <cite id="5">fundraising efficiency of $0.02 per $1 raised</cite> and a <cite id="10">program expense ratio of 89.8%</cite> in FY2023.
The organization holds a <cite id="4">100/100 overall score from Charity Navigator</cite>, including perfect marks for leadership and transparency.
In 2023 alone, IMRC successfully <cite id="11">distributed 10 million meals</cite> and provided medical care to <cite id="11">85,000 patients</cite>.

strengths_deep_dive: IMRC's primary strength lies in its long-term institutional presence in India, which allows for a <cite id="12">direct service delivery model</cite> rather than relying solely on third-party grants. This directness is paired with a <cite id="13">working capital ratio of 68 months</cite>, indicating a very stable reserve position that can sustain operations during funding fluctuations. Their healthcare infrastructure is particularly notable, having <cite id="14">treated over 118,000 patients</cite> in a single year through a network of clinics and hospitals. Furthermore, their <cite id="15">zakat program is comprehensive</cite>, covering categories from the poor (fuqara) to travelers in need (ibn sabil), ensuring religious compliance for donors.
rich_narrative.summary: Indian Muslim Relief and Charities (IMRC) operates as a significant humanitarian bridge between American donors and vulnerable minority communities in India. Founded in <cite id="1">1981</cite>, the organization has spent over four decades developing a direct service model that addresses systemic poverty through education, healthcare, and emergency relief. In FY2024, IMRC reported <cite id="2">$10,004,213 in total revenue</cite>, representing a <cite id="3">28% decline from the previous year</cite>. Despite this recent contraction in funding, the organization maintains a <cite id="4">perfect 100/100 rating from Charity Navigator</cite>, reflecting high standards of accountability. Their operations are characterized by high financial efficiency, spending only <cite id="5">$0.01 to raise every $1</cite>. This lean fundraising approach allows a larger portion of donations to reach the field. IMRC's impact is quantifiable across several sectors; for instance, they reported <cite id="6">educating 34,835 students</cite> and <cite id="7">treating 118,908 patients</cite> in their most recent annual reporting cycle. While the organization is highly effective at direct delivery, it currently lacks a <cite id="8">formally documented theory of change</cite>, which would help clarify the long-term causal pathways of its various interventions. For Muslim donors, IMRC offers a robust <cite id="9">zakat-eligible platform</cite> that serves eight specific asnaf categories, including the poor and needy.
